reader.requirement: At --std 85 a level-66 RENAMES entry (renaming an elementary item, a group, or a THRU range) has no true concept of level: it is not a subordinate of the record, adds nothing to the record's size or hierarchy, follows the record's last entry, and is itself no item of the record that another entry can rename (§1985:VI.5.11.3 SR2/SR4 state the consequences).

edition-consulted.switches: ClauseOperandsTakeImplicitQualifiers (Edition.DialectLevel >= 2002): from 2002 the RENAMES operand candidates are the record's own subtree (SubtreeCandidates, which never reaches a level-66 alias); below 2002 the whole scope's QualifiedCandidates, filtered by IsWithinRegion, which a level-66 alias of the same record passes

reader.edition-search: Read BindEntries' level-66 arm (the alias attaches to the owning record and never enters the level stack, edition-invariant), DataBinder.RenamesEntry.cs whole (no edition test), and ResolveRedefinesPass.Run's RENAMES loop; grepped DialectLevel in DataBinder.cs and found the one RENAMES-relevant switch at ClauseOperandsTakeImplicitQualifiers (kb/Work PB5165).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 a level-66 entry resolves as a RENAMES operand of a later 66 entry of the same record (accepted and run); at 2002/2023 it 'does not name an item of the record' (COBOL1655)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers a legal 66 THRU over two groups between other entries; not exercised: 66 over an elementary item, over one group, several 66 entries in a row, a FILE SECTION record, the record's size excluding 66 entries, and a 66 entry used as another 66's operand

reader.notes: The structural half conforms at 85: 66 aliases attach to the record without entering the level stack, take no storage, and a level entry after them is refused. The 85 arm of RegionClauseCandidates (PB5165's whole-scope candidates) finds the record's own level-66 alias by name, IsWithinRegion accepts it (its Parent is the record), and ScreenRenamesOperand bars only levels 1 and 77 because its comment assumes 66 and 88 are 'off the storage tree and already unreachable', which is true only of the 2002+ SubtreeCandidates arm. So at 85 a 66 entry is treated as a renamable item of the record.
